title: Last Occurrence
statement:
Given an unsorted array, answer t independent queries. For each value x, print its last 1-based position in the original array, or -1 if absent.

Input
The first line contains n and t. The next line contains n integers. The remaining input contains t query values.

Output
Print one answer per query, in query order.

Constraints
1 ≤ n, t ≤ 200000. All values are between -10⁹ and 10⁹.
editorial: Store (value, original position) pairs and sort them lexicographically. For query x, upper_bound((x,n)) points just past every occurrence of x. Check its predecessor exists and has value x. Its position is the largest original index. Sorting costs O(n log n), and t lookups cost O(t log n) total. Alternatively overwrite last[value] while reading the array. A set of values alone loses the positions.
